structured_output.what_is_happening: This is DEBT, an 11-minute-old token on PumpSwap. GMGN tags its launchpad as meteora_virtual_curve, and creation and migration happened at the same second. It is one of at least 10 same-ticker DEBT tokens launched within about 2 hours around one X post by Eric Bolling. Its GMGN website link points to a different DEBT contract (FYM6…, $359k market cap), which suggests this one is a copy. In about 15 minutes it went from launch to roughly $205k market cap, up about 300%. That came on about $290k of volume, 3,000 buys against 1,150 sells, and 1,629 unique buyers against only 74 unique sellers. The last 5 minutes carried more than half of all volume.

narrative.description: This is a copycat coin riding a live pump of the DEBT ticker. The story is 'national debt' plus Eric Bolling's post, which several teams launched on at the same time. The story itself has some political and macro-meme appeal, but it is split across many contracts.
narrative.why_spreading: One high-profile X post set off a copycat rush. Traders are rotating among the same-ticker contracts, and this one is catching overflow from the leaders at $838k and $359k.

token_connection.why_this_token: It carries the same ticker and cites the same Bolling post. Its own website link points to another DEBT contract (FYM6), so it is not the canonical token.
token_connection.competing_tokens: BLPK… DEBT COIN ($838k market cap, $1.2M hourly volume). FYM6… ($359k market cap, $4.2M hourly volume, the target of the usepaid link). 4Ptj… ($148k). tZNE… ($86k, launched after this one). Plus several dead variants.

authenticity.evidence: GMGN tags 41 bundler wallets and 9 snipers, and the bot/degen share is 12%. 1,629 unique buyers against only 74 unique sellers within 15 minutes is extreme and consistent with many small bot or bundle buys. There are no paid boosts, no smart-money wallets and no KOL wallets. Only 91 people have visited the GMGN page, which is low next to the transaction count.
authenticity.uncertainty: Without X data I can't tell whether real traders are rotating in from the leading DEBT contracts or whether bots are spraying buys across every copy.

structural_risks: RugCheck flags 99.99% of LP as unlocked (danger level), while GMGN reports lp_burn_ratio 1.0. The two sources disagree.
One unlabeled holder owns 80% of supply. GMGN's top-10 holder figure is 9.5%, so this is probably a pool or vault account, but that is not confirmed.
Liquidity is about $32k against a $205k market cap and heavy turnover.
It is a copy competing with larger same-ticker contracts.
The rally is already +300% at entry, so it is late in its first leg.

structured_output.counterargument: Meme rushes built on a news post can send several copies to multiples at once. At $205k it is cheaper than the $838k leader, and more than 1,600 buyers with few sellers in 15 minutes is strong demand. If the Bolling post keeps spreading, a rotation from the leaders could 2x this from entry.
unknowns: Whether the 80% holder is a pool/vault account or a single wallet
How far the Bolling post is actually reaching
Whether any DEBT contract gets endorsed as the official one

source_coverage.notes: No internet access in this condition. Judged from the evidence packet only.

structured_output.thesis: This is a non-canonical copy in a crowded same-ticker DEBT rush. It is already up about 300% at entry, with heavy bundler and bot activity and an odd ratio of buyers to sellers. Leftover rotation could give it spikes, but when a copycat rush fragments like this, the copies usually bleed out as attention settles on one or two leaders. A 2x before -50% is unlikely, though not negligible, given the high volatility.
